components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary operational action across forms, modals, and headers.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #0F6B5E); color: var(--accent-ink, #FFFFFF); padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 110ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-hover, #0B5449); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.975); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0F6B5E); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Supporting action such as Save as Draft or Itinerary preview.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--surface, #FFFFFF); color: var(--text-primary, #12171D); padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; border: 1px solid var(--border, #DFDDD4); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--surface-hover, #F7F6F1); border-color: var(--border-strong, #C9C5B9); }

components.description: Form input with emerald-teal focus ring.

narrative.overview:
TravelDesk is an operational corporate travel and expense portal designed around the clarity of an institutional treasury ledger and flight-plan folio. The interface rejects generic purple-indigo SaaS gradients in favor of warm alabaster paper in daylight and crisp obsidian slate in dark mode, anchored by a deep emerald-teal action voice.

Both themes prioritize fast queue scanning across four distinct roles (Employee, Manager, Finance, Admin). GSAP motion acts as spatial feedback — sliding segmented tab indicators, animated budget progress bars, smooth modal sheets, and drawn itinerary route tracks — while keeping content immediately visible and honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
keyCharacteristics: User-toggleable light ([data-theme="light"]) and dark ([data-theme="dark"]) themes persisted in localStorage.
Architectural summary strips and 3-column KPI bands paired with unified filter/search toolbars.
Tabular numeric alignment (tabular-nums) and JetBrains Mono reserved strictly for IDs, department codes, and timestamps.
Non-blocking GSAP choreography (power3.out, 180-320ms) with instant reduced-motion alternatives.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Status Rule
rules.body: Amber, burgundy, cobalt, and emerald status colors appear exclusively on badges, policy flags, and utilization thresholds — never as decorative backgrounds.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: Containment relies on 1px tonal borders (--border) rather than heavy drop shadows so dark and light modes share identical spatial hierarchy.

dos: Do use CSS custom properties (var(--surface), var(--text-primary), var(--border)) for every component state so both light and dark themes stay legible.
Do animate state transitions (tab switches, modals, inline drawers, itinerary route lines) with GSAP helpers from gsap.animations.ts and respect prefersReducedMotion().
Do use tabular-nums (.num) for every currency value, day count, percentage, and date column.
donts: Don't place one-sided border-left accent bars on rounded cards; use full borders, soft tinted badges, or leading icons.
Don't use raw browser alert() dialogs for API errors or confirmations; route notifications through ToastService.
Don't hardcode light-mode hex colors (#fafbfc, #fff) inside component stylesheets.
